correctness.rationale: For every real p>1, a in (0,1), b>0, eliminating scale in two explicit cycle equations yields the necessary and sufficient ratio identity a=(r^p-r)/(r^(p+1)-1). Substitution r=e^(2t) reduces its positive branch to sinh((p-1)t)/sinh((p+1)t). The monotone function H(u)=u coth(u) proves the ratio strictly decreases from (p-1)/(p+1) to zero; hence unique orbit exactly below threshold. For p=2, sum/product eliminate the orbit points, yielding explicit roots and the exact second-iterate multiplier 9a^2+6a-2. Its increasing polynomial crosses -1 once at (sqrt(2)-1)/3 and remains below 1 before the cycle disappears. The checker passed 1804 sampled tests, not used as infinite proof. At both neutral boundaries no nonlinear stability conclusion is made.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper raises a mathematically natural gap between mere existence of an innovation cycle and its dynamical stability. The theorem determines the exact count and coordinates of positive period-two states for every inverse-power exponent p>1, then identifies an independent sharp stability boundary for the analytically tractable and physically interpretable inverse-square exponent. The distinction between repelling oscillations (0<a<(sqrt(2)-1)/3) and attracting oscillations ((sqrt(2)-1)/3<a<1/3) is a substantive dynamical classification, not a routine numerical gain or trivial parameter substitution. It does not claim global attraction, arbitrary period classification, or economics outside the reduced model.
